title: 1-02 Northern Sea
body:
### Background and Hook(s)

- This is likely the first area explored by the players, and is tailored toward the first few level bands (3 - 7 and 5 - 9), meaning creatures with CR maxing out at about 8.

### Characters and Locations

- **Commander Vorthak ir’Ssar** (LE male sahuagin war captain, summit delegate). Broad-shouldered with jagged fin crests dyed crimson, and a deep scar running across his snout. Wears shark-tooth necklaces that clack ominously when he moves. Proud, quick to take offense, respects strength above diplomacy.

#### ★2: Gulf Stream (Syrania MZ)
 - [x]  ✅ 2026-02-16
>The water here is impossibly clear and warm, flowing in a steady, vertical spiral that lifts you as much as it carries you forward. Pale ribbons of light drift upward like lazy banners, humming softly as they pass. Loose debris does not sink or rise — it _orbits_, tracing slow halos in the water. Far below, shapes like marble platforms and broken arches hang upside-down, as if gravity forgot which way was down. The stream continues past them, descending into bright blue nothing.

- This area is a low-threat, high-temptation manifest zone to Syrania. The danger is not immediate violence; it is disorientation, separation, and the lure of things that are hard to reach but clearly valuable.
- One obvious draw is aerostatic wreckage: fragments of skyships, elemental rings, or Aereni sky-platforms that were never meant to be underwater but now hover, slowly rotating, held aloft by Syranian gravity bleed. These can be scavenged safely only by leaving the vessel, because the current around them is too turbulent for docking. Importantly, these wrecks should look intact and reachable, not crushed—this signals reward rather than hazard.
	- Roll on the [[C06 The City Between#Random Discovery|Random Discovery]] table to determine what's found here.
- Another strong enticement is current-locked fauna. Schools of translucent fish or ray-like creatures ride the vertical flow endlessly. One or two are visibly carrying something artificial embedded in their bodies: rings, gemstones, dragonshards, etc (ask a player to fill in the details). They are not hostile, but they cannot be interacted with from a distance.
- **Environment**: DC 12

>[!danger]- **Thermal Updraft (Environmental Lair Action)**
>Creatures in the lowest vertical band are gently carried upward. Each affected creature moves one vertical band upward unless it spends half of its movement to stabilize itself. Objects not secured drift upward automatically.

>[!danger]- **Buoyancy Collapse (Environmental Lair Action)**  
Any creature that moves more than one range band since its last turn, or that interacts physically with a floating structure, must succeed on a Dexterity (Acrobatics) check or lose neutral buoyancy, drifting one vertical band at the end of the round or exploration beat.

#### ★2: Hal'syra
 - [x]  ✅ 2026-05-18
- This is the center for commerce and trade with other cultures. Hal’syra even has a rarely-used quadrant enchanted so surface dwellers can breathe within it. This city is the source of the ambassadors, envoys, and merchants who deal with surface dwellers and other cultures, and it’s here that the scholars of the Ta’har study surface dwellers and debate the best ways to deal with them.
- These major cities are each home to hundreds of thousands of sahuagin, and the total population of the Dominion is well into the millions. Farms and other small communities scattered between the great cities are often largely inhabited by locathah, with a core group of sahuagin overlords. In between, there are large stretches with no humanoid population; here, ruins of the giants and remnants of other fallen civilizations might be found.
- **Commander Vorthak ir’Ssar**, as chief diplomat (as much as that means to them) of the sahuagin, is found here. He can explain anything about the sahuagin, their cities, and their culture.
- **Beacons of Passage** — common magic items that tell the sahuagin their travel is authorized, charged to last for a set time. The players may be able to negotiate for limited or even completely free passage in sahuagin waters.

#### ★2: The Omnipus
 - [ ]  
- The Omnipus dwells here — a huge octopus with an incredible intelligence due to its nine large brains (one in its head and one in each of its tentacles). Each tentacle brain holds all of the details of one of the oceans of Eberron (minus the Bitter Sea and Iceflow Sea, which aren't used in this campaign), and his head holds any information about the land.
- The players can negotiate to learn any information they may want about any area of the world (or roll a d8 to get a random result), but each brain requires a separate Persuasion check - with the DC based on the difficulty of the area (which also serves as a hint of escalating difficulty for these areas). Any failed Persausion checks result in a tentacle slap (1d8 bludgeoning damage).
	- **Barren Sea** (DC 15): Random Encounters (CR ~10 involving draconic and psionic-empowered creatures)
	- **Dark Sea** (DC 18): Random Encounters (CR ~16 involving dragons and darkness), Kuo-toa Settlement/Ruins, Valraean Protectorate, Abyssal Protectorate
	- **Dragonreach** (DC 17): Random Encounters (CR ~15 involving dragons and elves), Maraen Sea Elf Settlement, Dragon Turtle Feeding/Breeding Grounds
	- **Lhazaar Sea** (DC 13): Port Kraz (Lhazaar), Hal'Kyth
	- **Sea of Lost Souls** (DC 16): Random Encounters (CR ~11 involving undead and charm/calls)
	- **Sea of Rage** (DC 20): Aventi homeland only - not technically part of the point crawl right now (but could be added if the PCs want)
	- **Thunder Sea** (DC 12): Sahuagin territory and home to at least half a dozen sar'lassa (and their associated manifest zones), half a dozen ports, Gundbarg (Koalinth Redoubt), Demonsong Channel and Aboleth Temple
	- **White Sea** (DC 14): Random Encounters (CR ~7 involving cold and ice)
	- **Land** (DC 20): Anything about port cities outside of the docks, or any inland cities or locations.

#### ★7: Fracture Reaches (Xoriat MZ)
 - [x]  ✅ 2026-05-18
>The water here bends wrong, thickening in places and thinning in others, as if distance itself can’t decide how much it weighs. Shapes repeat where they shouldn’t—your ship’s silhouette echoes behind you, then ahead, then sideways—while distant clicking sounds arrive before their source. Coral grows in spirals that hurt to focus on, and patches of water ripple like exposed nerves. Every so often, something large moves just out of sync with the rest of the sea.

- This zone should feel actively wrong, not merely dangerous. Unlike Syrania (inviting) or Risia (restraining), Xoriat is provocative. It doesn’t just exist; it interferes. The players should feel watched, misjudged, and tested. What draws them out of the ship should be things that look unstable but significant—evidence that something should not be here, and might get worse if ignored.
- One strong draw is living terrain. Reefs that pulse faintly like organs, membranes stretched between rock spires, or coral lattices that slowly reconfigure themselves when not directly observed. These structures often contain cavities—nests, growth nodes, or “scar tissue” where aberrations gestate. They cannot be meaningfully interacted with from a vessel; proximity matters.
- Another enticement is false landmarks. Ruins that resemble known cultures (Aereni arches, sahuagin totems, Couaxolotl motifs) but are subtly wrong—too symmetrical, mirrored inside-out, or grown rather than built. These are bait: places where the players expect safety, knowledge, or relics, only to realize the environment is imitating memory.
	- Roll on the [[C06 The City Between#Random Discovery|Random Discovery]] table to determine what's found here.
- You should also include aberrant activity tells. Trails of disturbed water that move against currents, schools of fish swimming in synchronized geometric patterns, or areas where sound dampens unnaturally. These signal that combat is possible but not guaranteed—the players can choose whether to engage, observe, or retreat.
- **Environment**: DC 14

>[!danger]- **Spatial Slippage (Environmental Lair Action)**  
Choose one creature that moved this round. That creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or appear in a different but adjacent vertical or horizontal range band of the environment’s choice. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.

>[!danger]- **Aberrant Echoes (Environmental Lair Action)**  
Until initiative count 20 next round, the first time a creature makes an attack roll or casts a spell, a distorted echo manifests. That creature must succeed on an Intelligence saving throw or suffer disadvantage on its next attack roll or saving throw as its perceptions briefly misalign.

>[!danger]- **Gestational Rupture (Environmental Lair Action)**
If two or more creatures have failed saving throws caused by the environment since the last round, a nearby growth tears open. One aberrant creature (appropriate to tier) emerges in an unoccupied adjacent range band and acts on the next initiative count.

`encounter: 1: Chuul`

#### ★7: Hal'xor (Temple of Tentacles)
 - [x]  ✅ 2026-05-18
- This is the first true Deep One cult site that the PCs are likely to encounter. The cult are a minor sect attempted to communicate with the slowly emerging Overlord, and are unaware of the kuo-toa connection to this emergence - they are strictly opportunists.
- **Temple of Tentacles General Features**:
	- **Unholy Engravings**. Inside, the temple is covered with profane carvings of tentacle-armed men, and fractured, sacrilegious hieroglyphics. Characters who look upon the bas-reliefs must make a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw, becoming frightened on a failed saving throw. If the saving throw fails by 5 or more, the character also gains a form of short-term madness, determined by rolling on the Short Term Madness table in chapter 8 of the DMG.
	- **Nearby Karlassa**. Occasionally, a deep tremor shakes the entire structure — consistent with a gargantuan seabed creature shifting nearby, with no sign of intelligence or intent.
	- **Constellation Chamber**. The dungeon contains a machine which can be used to replicate constellations, found in area T5. The machine is currently set to Chronepsis, which gives all characters in this dungeon disadvantage on Wisdom and Charisma saving throws.

##### T1. Temple Entry
>A domed granite structure rises from the water, carved to resemble a colossal squid standing upright on spiraling tentacles. Barnacles and kelp cling to the stone, and dark seawater flows in and out through narrow gaps between the limbs. A crucified corpse — twisted, partially transformed, and unmistakably not fully humanoid — hangs near the main opening, swaying gently with the tide.

- Entry is partially submerged; swimming or underwater movement required.
- **Corpse**. Characters who see the corpse (Deep One hybrid used as a threshold ward) must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw, becoming frightened on a failed saving throw. If the saving throw fails by 5 or more, the character also gains a form of short-term madness, determined by rolling on the Short Term Madness table in chapter 8 of the DMG.
- Characters who succeed on a DC 18 Intelligence (Nature) check can determine that the creature is some foreign aberration from the fathoms below. A successful DC 18 Wisdom (Medicine) check reveals that the creature died several weeks ago and has been hung here since.
- **Treasure**. There are is a handful of corals and shells exquisitely carved to resemble starfish (300 gp) beneath the corpse.

##### T2. Aquatic Antechamber
>The passage slopes down into a low stone chamber where seawater pools waist-deep, swirling in slow circles as it drains through grooves cut into the floor. The air above the waterline is cold and stale, carrying a sour reek of kelp and old incense. Spiral carvings crawl across the walls, slick with condensation, and a low hum presses behind your eyes, steady and patient.

- **Psychic Pressure**. Must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom save or disadvantage on Perception checks here.
- **Secret Door**. Characters who succeed on a DC 16 Wisdom (Perception) check feel a breeze coming from the north corner of the eastern wall. Characters who succeed on a DC 16 Intelligence (Investigation) check discover that the breeze comes from a secret door, which can be opened by depressing a certain stone in the wall.

##### T3. Subterranean Shrine
>The passage opens into a broad cavern where the stone has been worn smooth by ancient tides. Green-black slime coats the walls and floor, and a massive altar of worked stone rises at the far end, faintly glowing. The water vibrates with a slow, rhythmic thrum that feels less like sound than thought.

- **Ledge**. In the southwest of the cavern is a 20-foot high rock shelf that leads to area T6. Characters with a passive Wisdom (Perception) of 18 or higher can hear whispering sounds from the tunnel (see area T6).
- **Statues**. Each of the statues is covered by a thick layer of the harmless green ooze. Clearing away the slime reveals horrific mutations of the human form rendered in jet-black stone. The figures are humanoid in form, but have dozens of thin, drooping tentacles where their faces should be. Fins sprout from their limbs, and their skin has a distinctly scabrous quality. The base of the statues reads, ‘Yogg Fh’leydn – The Sufferers’.
	- The statues are psychically linked to the ochre jellies in the room, with any damage dealt to the oozes instead split between the three statues (AC 17; 25 HP; immunity to cold, fire, poison, and psychic damage; and resistance to non-magical physical damage). When the statues take damage, they cry like a struck animal.
	- The connection is broken if a statue is destroyed, or if targeted with dispel magic (DC 15). If a statue is destroyed it emits a hideous scream. Each creature within 30 feet of the statue that can hear it must succeed on a DC 10 Wisdom saving throw or gain a random form of short-term madness, determined by rolling on the Short-Term Madness table (chapter 8 of the DMG).
- **Creatures**. There are five starfish-shaped ochre jellies in the chamber, one in each of the five ooze-filled alcoves. These jellies are psychically linked to the statues. They attack any creature that walks past them.
- **Altar**. At the eastern end of the cavern is a 5-foot tall plinth atop which is an altar of green stone. On the altar is a +2 dagger made of coral, a [[ring of free action]] and two copper chalices with silver filigrees depicting strange, tentacled humanoids (25 gp each). The altar is currently glowing a faint purple (see area T5). On either side of the altar are two tapestries degraded by mold and smeared green ooze. Drawing the southern tapestry aside reveals a descending tunnel leading to T4. Characters with a passive Wisdom (Perception) of 18 or higher can hear whispering sounds from behind it (see area T6).

`encounter: 5: Ochre Jelly`

##### T4. Store Chamber
>Little of worth remains in this storeroom. The dozen or so wooden crates here are covered with a brown, fungous sheet.

- **Brown Mold**. Growing over each crate in the room is a sheet of brown mold (chapter 5 of the DMG). https://www.5esrd.com/database/creature/brown-mold/
- **Crates**. Characters who succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation) check notice that four of the crates are intact and might contain goods. The crates are nailed shut and require a successful DC 12 Strength check to open. The crates contain the following:
	1) Six robes embroidered with a seaweed and tentacle design around the arms (5 gp each).
	2) Fourteen boxes containing ten candles each (1 cp per candle).
	3) A set of navigator’s tools (25 gp), a brass spyglass covered in verdigris that is always cold to the touch (1,000 gp), three books of astrology and astronomy (25 gp each), and hundreds of pieces of parchment detailing constellations and complex star maps.
	4) A bronze gong (15 gp), three feet in diameter, a hammer with which to hit it, and a small wooden box with a bronze kraken clasp. Inside the box is a [[ring of shooting stars]]. The ring is cursed; any creature attuned to it gains vulnerability to psychic damage.

##### T5. Constellation Chamber
>Three wheel-like mechanisms of tarnished metal are anchored to the stone floor, all copper balls and thin steel rods, each fitted with a crank and chain. The walls of the chamber display a myriad of constellations rendered in shells and corals

- Both stone doors to this chamber are locked. The keys are kept by The Listener in area T6. The doors can be unlocked with a successful DC 18 Dexterity check using thieves’ tools, or smashed down with a successful DC 16 Strength check.
- **Contraptions**. Each of the three wheels can be rotated using the crank and chain. The position of the balls can be made to match three different constellation patterns or scrambled to match none. Characters with knowledge of the stars, or who have discovered the books and parchment in the crates in area T4, can attempt an Intelligence check to interpret the machinery. Depending on the result of the check, the character gains different information:
	- 0-10. The character understands nothing.
	- 11-14. The character believes the machinery can be rotated to resemble constellations, though they don’t recognize any of them.
	- 15-18. The character realizes they can rotate the wheels to break the current constellation.
	- 19+. The character knows the machinery is currently depicting a constellation called Chronepsis. The wheels can be rotated to form Garyx and Astilabor. Chronepsis is a constellation, involving fate and prophesy. Garyx is associated with chaos and destruction. Astilabor is said to be a good omen; a promise of riches to come.
- The characters can use the cranks to change the constellation, doing so has the following effects:
	- No Constellation. The Deep One Priests in area T8 lose their damage resistances. The altar in area T3 stops glowing.
	- Chronepsis (fate/prophecy). Creatures in the dungeon have disadvantage on Wisdom and Charisma saving throws. The altar in area T3 glows purple.
	- Garyx (chaos/destruction). Creatures in the dungeon have advantage on attack rolls and Wisdom (Survival) checks. The altar in area T3 glows red.
	- Astilabor (wealth). Anything that touches the altar in area T3 turns to solid gold. If a nonmagical object touches the altar it turns to gold and loses all functionality. If a creature touches the altar, it must succeed on a DC 20 Constitution saving throw against being magically petrified. On a failed save, the creature begins to turn to gold and is restrained. It must repeat the saving throw at the end of its next turn. On a success, the effect ends. On a failure, the creature is petrified and is transformed into solid gold. The altar in area T3 glows yellow.

##### T6. The Listener
>As you travel down the tunnel, you pick up on the sound of whispered conversation. Rounding a corner, you notice a mildew-covered canvas has been nailed into the natural stone wall. The source of the whispering is clearly behind it.

- **The Listener**. Whispering to herself behind the canvas is The Listener (CN female kuo-toa cleric) - a failed cult conduit who attempted to “hear” the Deep One through the constellation rites and broke (deafening herself with a dagger in order to escape the ritual hum and constant whispering). She suffers from madness, and must be calmed before any attempt at communication (DC 18 Persuasion, or a spell that calms emotions or removes madness).
	- Knows the layout, warns of the priests below, and understands that the constellation chamber “draws the Deep One closer.”
	- Holds keys to T5 and carries a [[potion of healing]] (greater).

##### T7. Guard Quarters
>This chamber is bare and utilitarian, with weighted nets, stone shelves, and a single tethered sleeping pallet. It feels recently abandoned, as though its occupants were summoned away without warning.

- No fixed encounter; suitable for patrols or a risky short rest. Minor supplies and personal effects reinforce the cult’s routine nature.

##### T8. Sanctum of the Deep One Priests
>A wide chamber opens onto a stone platform overlooking a narrow, black cleft in the seabed. Spiral runes ring the fissure, and robed figures drift in slow, deliberate motions, chanting in a wet, bubbling cadence that vibrates through your bones. The water near the cleft feels thick, as if pressed from the far side by something vast and patient.

- Occupied by Deep One cult priests. This is a ritual sanctum for communion and invocation, not summoning a creature into the space.
- **Deep One Circle**. If encountered together in the temple, the five Deep One Priests can each cast the following spells from the warlock’s spell list but must share the spell slots among themselves:
	- Cantrips (at will): [[eldritch blast]], [[minor illusion]], [[prestidigitation]], [[thunderclap]]
	- 1st-5th level (3 5th-level slots): [[arms of hadar]], [[banishment]], [[counterspell]], [[crown of madness]], [[darkness]], [[dream]], [[enthrall]], [[fear]], [[hallucinatory terrain]], [[hunger of hadar]], [[witch bolt]]
	- For casting these spells, each kraken priest is a 12th-level spellcaster that uses Wisdom as its spellcasting ability (spell save DC 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks)

`encounter: 5: Deep One Priest`

#### ★8: Iceberg Floats (Risia MZ)
 - [x]  ✅ 2026-04-13
>The water temperature drops abruptly, numbing exposed skin as the sea turns a deep, glassy blue. Above and below you drift massive icebergs, some inverted, some cracked open like cathedral vaults, their undersides glowing faintly with cold blue light. Each iceberg sheds slow snowfalls of frost that sink rather than rise, hissing softly as they dissolve. The current here is sluggish, heavy, and silent, as if sound itself has frozen.

- The ship can navigate carefully, but many of the most interesting features are inaccessible without exiting: fissures in the ice, frozen inclusions, and slow-moving phenomena that cannot be interacted with mechanically from a vessel. What draws the players out are things trapped in ice, not things drifting freely.
- The strongest draw is preserved wreckage. Ships, constructs, or creatures are frozen mid-motion inside translucent ice, perfectly intact. Some are clearly ancient, others disturbingly recent. These are not crushed or decayed; they are paused. Players immediately understand that whatever is inside can be recovered—but only if they physically reach the ice and work on it.
	- Roll on the [[C06 The City Between#Random Discovery|Random Discovery]] table to determine what's found here.
- Another compelling feature is cold-light inclusions: veins of glowing crystal, dragonshards, or planar frost embedded deep within the icebergs. The light refracts strangely, bending around corners, suggesting depth and richness that cannot be harvested at range. These inclusions can resonate with magic, pearls, or elemental engines, giving you an easy hook for noncombat interaction.
- A third option is Risian fauna. Slow-moving, pale creatures cling to the ice or drift between bergs, barely moving. They are not aggressive unless disturbed, but their stillness is unsettling. Some are clearly predators adapted to ambush anything warm enough to matter. Again, the message is subtle danger, not an immediate fight.
- **Environment**: DC 13

>[!danger]- **Thermal Drain (Environmental Lair Action)**  
Each creature not protected from extreme cold that ends its turn or action cycle outside a vehicle must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have its speed reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn. This effect stacks. A creature whose speed is reduced to 0 in this way also loses neutral buoyancy.

>[!danger]- **Frozen Stillness (Environmental Lair Action)**  
Until initiative count 20 on the next round (or the next exploration beat), creatures that did not move since their last turn have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks and checks made to resist forced movement. Creatures that moved more than one range band this round have disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws.

#### ★8: Hal'ris
 - [ ]  
>The water here is painfully cold, clear enough to see a vast shape entombed below—an immense kar’lassa locked in layered ice and unmoving brine. Frosted currents spiral slowly around it, tugging at loose silt and whispering through cracks in the frozen mass. Dark shapes hover at a careful distance: sentries who do not patrol, but wait. Farther out, faint marker-stones and shell-etched floats trace subtle survey lines.

- The kar’lassa bound to Risia is not inert. It is actively suppressing itself, freezing its own bodily processes to avoid triggering... something. The sahuagin never built a city here.
- **The Stillward Sahuagin**. A small, ostracized sect of sahuagin known informally as the Stillward maintains a perpetual watch over the dormant Risia kar’lassa. They believe the Eternal Dominion’s refusal to build here is cowardice — that witnessing the dreamer’s eventual awakening is a sacred obligation, even if it never comes in their lifetime.
- **The Locathah Survey**. Operating at the edge of the site is a locathah survey cell, carefully mapping the waters, thermal changes, and current anomalies caused by the stasis field. The locathah believe Hal’ris is slowly destabilizing, but they will not approach closer than their markers allow.
- **Potential Conflict**. The Stillward believe the locathah’s measurements risk provoking the kar’lassa by “measuring the dream too closely.” The locathah believe the sahuagin’s constant presence is masking early warning signs of a catastrophic thaw. Neither side wants violence; both fear being blamed if something goes wrong.
- The PCs may encounter:
	- A tense standoff over the removal or relocation of a single survey marker that has drifted closer to the ice than intended.
	- Conflicting interpretations of recent data: the locathah see a slow warming trend; the Stillward insist it is cyclical and sacred.
	- A mutual but unspoken fear that if Hal’ris does begin to awaken, the Eternal Dominion will erase everyone involved.

#### ♦2: Gundbarg (Koalinth Redoubt)
 - [x]  ✅ 2026-03-16
- Koalinth were developed by the goblinoid Empire of Dhakaan to defend the coastline, though the dar never sought to cross the sea. These aquatic hobgoblins were exterminated by the sahuagin following the collapse of the empire, though koalinth tribes are occasionally discovered in remote locations. It’s possible a more sophisticated clan of koalinth went into deep seclusion at the same time as other Kech Dhakaan; if so, this could be an interesting ally for the Heirs of Dhakaan.
- Gundbarg is a nearly-forgotten koalinth redoubt carved into a broken coastal shelf, the last remnant of a people engineered for a war they ultimately lost. Most of the original Dhakaani structure lies flooded beneath the surf; what remains is a handful of reinforced stone buildings, a submerged hall, and a single working beacon. The koalinth here endure through discipline and memory rather than numbers, maintaining watch not because they expect help, but because abandonment is how their people died.

##### Locations
- **Saltwood Storehouse.** A squat stone warehouse sealed with resin and iron bands, smelling permanently of brine and rot. It holds preserved kelp, dried fish, salvaged supplies, and a carefully guarded stock of alchemical goods; Granny Saltwood controls access and knows exactly what she can spare — and what price she will ask.
- **Gimlet’s Ship Repairs**. A rough dock built into a natural cleft, capable of patching hulls, reinforcing keels, and fitting temporary underwater modifications. The koalinth shipwrights here are blunt and efficient, demanding materials or favors rather than coin.
- **The Tide Hall**. A partially submerged Dhakaani chamber used for councils, drills, and remembrance. Its worn reliefs depict koalinth defending coastlines alongside goblinoid legions, reinforcing the city’s identity as a remnant of a larger, vanished war machine.
- **Stone Lighthouse**. An ancient Dhakaani beacon tower rising from the rocks, its green-blue flame maintained by ritual rather than fuel. It serves as Gundbarg’s early warning system and last line of defense, and its keepers have recently reported movement near old sea caves along the coast.

##### Characters
- **Granny Saltwood** (female sea hag, disguised as a koalinth). Sharp-eyed, irritable, and fiercely pragmatic, Granny Saltwood controls Gundbarg’s remaining supplies and alchemical stock. She possesses the knowledge to brew potions of water breathing, but requires rare reagents rumored to lie in nearby sea caves (Gallows Grotto) — an obvious problem she is willing to outsource.
- **Kethra** (female koalinth, watch-captain). A scarred, disciplined veteran who oversees patrols and lighthouse rotations. She views outsiders as temporary tools, not allies, but respects competence and follow-through.
- **Urzak** (male koalinth, lorekeeper). Old and methodical, Urzak preserves Dhakaani records, koalinth oral history, and sealed relic inventories. He is cautious but quietly hopeful that contact with the Heirs of Dhakaan might mean something other than extinction.
- **Tressa Coilwake** (female human, coastal salvager). A tolerated outsider granted temporary shelter, Tressa brings news, rumors, and small trade goods from the surface. She knows the coastline well enough to confirm that the sea caves near the lighthouse are active — and dangerous.

#### ♦2: Gallows Grotto
 - [x]  ✅ 2026-03-16
- **Gallows Grotto General Features**. The following aspects of Gallows Grotto are true unless otherwise noted in a particular area description:
	- **Ceilings**. The caverns within Gallows Grotto are thirty feet tall.
	- **Desecrated Ground**. Due to the dark past of the caves, Gallows Grotto is considered desecrated ground (see chapter 5 of the Dungeon Master’s Guide).
	- **Light**. The caves are entirely dark and unlit. 
	- **Slick Rock**. The floor of the caves is wet with salt spray. A creature that takes the Dash action within Gallows Grotto must make a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw at the start of their move or fall prone. The walls cannot be climbed without gear, and even characters with gear must succeed on a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check in order to do so.

##### G1. Entrance Cavern
- The cavern is haunted by a specter which attacks good aligned creatures that enter.

`encounter: Specter`

##### G2. Sea Lion Den
>A natural stair of wet rocks leads up toward a cave which reeks of fish. Peering inside, you notice the slumbering hulk of a vicious beast. The front of the creature is that of a scaled, green lion, but its hindquarters have been replaced by the tail of a giant fish. The creature is over ten feet long and has a chain around its neck. Strewn around the monstrosity are handfuls of fish guts. As you watch, the massive beast’s nostrils begin to flare.

- This sea lion has a badly scarred front flipper. It belongs belongs to Granny Saltwood, and has the following changes:
	- The sea lion has 50 hit points.
	- The sea lion has a swim speed of 20 ft.
	- The sea lion loses multiattack.
- The sea lion wears a hag eye (see Monster Manual) on a chain collar. Granny Saltwood can see through the eye. If the characters don’t discover the sea lion it remains asleep unless they enter area G4, when it is magically awakened and waits to ambush them.
- Characters is area G2 must take immediate action to avoid waking the sea lion. They can retreat entirely from the cave or mask their scent using the offal or a spell such as *prestidigitation*. If they fail to do so, the sea lion wakes up and attacks, trying to knock characters into the water where it is most deadly.

`encounter: 1: Sea Lion`

##### G3. Seaweed Sanctuary
>A still rockpool of saltwater fills the majority of this cavern. Growing within it are a dozen kinds of seaweed.

- **Dead Man’s Bootlaces**. A character can identify the seaweed with a successful DC 10 Intelligence (Nature) check, made with advantage if the characters have a sample. Alternatively, a character can make a DC 12 Intelligence (History) check to recall being shown the sample by Granny Saltwood. A failed check could result in the characters procuring the wrong variety. If the wrong variety is taken to Granny Saltwood, she still makes the potions for them, but they receive potions of poison instead.

Characters can prevent the ritual by depriving them or their sight or ability to speak in any way, breaking the caster’s concentration, or by casting *counterspell* as the ritual comes to its conclusion.
- **Trapped Stairs**. The stairs closest the door are trapped. Stepping on the top stair causes the stairs to tilt, turning them into a slide. At the same time, a 10-foot square pit filled with green fire swings open at the bottom of the stairs. Any creature on the stairs when the trap is triggered must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or slide down into the pit. When a creature enters the pit for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, that creature takes `dice:4d10` fire damage. Characters with a passive Wisdom (Perception) of 18 or higher notice the trap, and can avoid the top step.
- **Ceiling & Levels**. The ceiling of this chamber is 50 feet tall. The platform is 20 feet tall.

`encounter: 1: Star Spawn Mangler`

##### A21. Hall of Six Statues
>This wide chamber is bordered by midnight black columns in stoas. In the center of the chamber are six identical statues of green stone. The horrendous forms sculpted in stone vomit forth twisting black beams of energy.

- **Statues**. Each statue can be rotated using an action. The beams continue until they hit a statue, wall, column or creature. Overlapping beams has no additional effect. A creature hit by the beam is targeted by a ray of enfeeblement (DC 20). If the beams hit a pillar, they shoot across horizontally to close off the sides of the chamber with a wall of fire (DC 20). If a beam hits a statue, it stops. By rotating the statues different symbols can be made using the beams. The different symbols cause different effects (see appendix E for the symbols):
	- Symbol A. A chuul is summoned between the central pillars.
	- Symbol B. Both doors on the eastern wall unlock.
	- Symbol C. Each creature in the room is subjected to the slow spell (DC 20), which lasts for 1 minute.
	- Symbol D. A doppelganger of each creature appears in the room in a mirrored position (as if creating symmetry down the central line).
	- Symbol E. Each creature in the room is subjected to the haste spell, which lasts for 1 minute.
- **Doors**. The doors on the eastern wall are both locked, and can only be opened by making the required symbol:
	- Left-Hand Door. The left-hand door is magically trapped. Any creature that opens the door sees an illusion of a cavernous tunnel beyond created by the silent image spell (DC 20). A creature that steps through is teleported to area A22, though the illusion responds as if they had walked through.
	- Right-Hand Door. The floor of the corridor is subject to a permanent spike growth spell (DC 20).
- **Ceiling & Levels**. The chamber is 30 feet tall. The levels by the door are 20-feet high.

`encounter: 1: Chuul`

##### A22. Aboleth Lair
>The circular chamber before you is formed of featureless iridescent metal. The center of the chamber is entirely composed of a huge pool of water, in which a large shadow swims slowly in the depths. A fragmented stone causeway lies submerged beneath the pool’s surface, broken into uneven slabs and half-collapsed arches. A narrow outer ledge traces the chamber wall just above the waterline, slick with algae and mineral runoff. Both seem as though they could lead to the door on the far side of the pool.

- **Crossing Options**. Players may decide to take the submerged walkway (moving slab to slab just barely beneath the water), or the outer ledge (careful sidling along the chamber wall). Either route requires 3 successful Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks before 2 failures. On the first failure, the character slips, stumbles, or loses progress. On the second failure, the character falls into the water and the aboleth moves toward to attack (except Maris, who it will never attack).
- **Watery Projections**. At the start of each character’s turn while crossing, they must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, the character is distracted by visions reflected on the water’s surface and has disadvantage on their next Dexterity check. When a character fails this save, ask the player to briefly describe what their character sees (memory, sermon, vision, or moment of “faith”). These visions should escalate in clarity for Maris specifically (see visions at start of adventure).
- **Aboleth Behavior**. The aboleth does not attack unless provoked and does not interfere physically. If attacked, it defends itself but does not pursue characters who retreat - and it will never attack Maris, under any circumstances.
- **Psionic Crystals**. If the Psionic Crystal in A6 hasn't been destroyed, then the aboleth has *sanctuary* cast on it, requiring a Wisdom saving throw (DC 16) before being able to target it with a damaging effect. If the Psionic Crystal in A17 hasn't been destroyed, then the aboleth has *death ward* cast on it, saving it from death once.

`encounter: 1: Aboleth`

>Smooth stone walls curve inward, etched with shallow spirals that catch and distort the low light, drawing the eye toward a central altar rising from the floor. Resting atop it is a large, clouded aboleth eye, preserved in a thin layer of musuc, faintly luminous and watching without blinking.

- Resting on the central alter is a Preserved Aboleth Eye (clouded, lidless, faintly warm to the touch) that serves as an arcane focus for Maris - giving one extra pact slot per day. #### ⚔1: Dal Quor Scar
 - [ ]  
- An unremarkable stretch of open ocean with nothing to mark it — except navigation feels slightly wrong, dreaming creatures avoid it, and the water has an ashen quality. This is where Dal Quor was last coterminous before the severance. No faction knows what it is.
